Could the pedestrian timer be shortened or the green light for cars turning from Inman onto Mass Ave be delayed? Pedestrians walking on Mass Ave invariably try to cross Inman even if the display only shows "1", which puts them in the middle of the road when the light for cars on Inman turns green. It endangers those pedestrians but also causes honking and aggravation for drivers, which probably has a non-negligible safety effect when those drivers, delayed by the pedestrians, then speed through that intersection and future intersections. Separating the pedestrian crossing signal from the green light by 2-3 seconds -- which the City does at so many other intersections, which is great -- would allow pedestrians to clear the street before cars start to go. I'm not sure there's another way to stop pedestrians from pushing the limits of when they can cross right up until the countdown ends, so ending the timer earlier or delaying the green by 2-3 seconds seems like the best solution.
